22:51 < jal0> the problem with that idea, is that the display also uses an irq, by remapping ALL irqs, you have no way of knowing whats going on
22:51 < someguy> don't some of the interrupts need to be cleared before returning once they are called
22:52 < jal0> yeap
22:52 < jal0> thats the other problem
22:52 < antagonizt> cli
22:52 < jal0> then no irqs will be printed
22:53 < jal0> if you cli from within the interrupt, only the highest priority interrupt would ever be called
22:57 < jal0> generaly speaking external interrupt devices are attached to the micro in a wired-or configuration. it is the responsibility of the interrupt handler to ask each device in turn "were you interrupted" if not it continues to the next lower irq source.
22:58 < jal0> if the device says "yes" then a call is made to the device specific irq handler which figures out what happend being that most external devices have more than one interrupt source
22:59 < jal0> once determined that specifice irq handler is called which services the device and clears the irq source.
22:59 < jal0> hope this helps on VERY BASICALY how irq's work
